_comment: Street RBA calls (economists and strategists). Update when an institution changes its view. For each bank: next_meeting = the RBA decision date the call refers to; call = hike | no change | cut; next_change = {month: YYYY-MM, optional label for approximate timing e.g. 'Mid 2027', direction: hike | cut, size_bp, rate_after}; as_of = date of the source; sources = links, newest first (the call bubble on the page links to sources[0], so put the article the current call comes from first). Set call to null if the bank has not published a view for the next meeting.

banks.note: Savings.com.au (25 Nov, after October CPI at 4.9% headline, 3.8% trimmed mean): major bank economists expect the RBA to hold next month; 'CBA, NAB, and Westpac likewise forecast rate cuts next year, albeit at a later timing for the first move, in August'. Belinda Allen (CommBank) also said December was unlikely to be a 'live' meeting (Trading and Investment News, 25 Nov). Earlier: Allen (MPA 19 Nov): 'An on-hold decision in December is locked in for the RBA'; cuts pencilled in for August and November 2027

Westpac October CPI quick take (ActionForex, 25 Nov): October was 'a shade above our nowcast'; the board 'will be in something of a holding pattern at next month's meeting', the RBA is 'likely finished hiking rates', and 'the most likely date for the first interest rate cut is August next year'. Savings.com.au (25 Nov): CBA, NAB and Westpac forecast the first cut in August. Earlier, Luci Ellis (13 Nov): 'A rate hike in February 2027 cannot be ruled out but it is looking even less likely'

Savings.com.au (25 Nov, after October CPI at 4.9%): major bank economists expect a December hold; 'CBA, NAB, and Westpac likewise forecast rate cuts next year, albeit at a later timing for the first move, in August'. NAB economists said October 'would likely mark the peak for headline inflation'; Taylor Nugent: housing 'an unlikely source of persistent inflation pressure' (AAP, 25 Nov). Earlier, Sally Auld (23 Nov): 'we think the RBA is done hiking'; NAB expects the RBA to hold in December

Savings.com.au (25 Nov, after October CPI at 4.9%): major bank economists expect a December hold; ANZ keeps its first cut in June 2027 (brought forward from November 2027), saying 'any easing cycle will depend on underlying inflation continuing to move towards the RBA's target band'; AAP (25 Nov): ANZ 'stuck with their timing for a first rate cut in June'. Earlier, Adam Boyton (24 Nov): 25bp to 4.60% in June, then August 2027 and February 2028 to 4.10%

Shane Oliver (AMP weekly update for the week of 20 Nov, via Livewire; page undated): RBA 'likely to remain on hold at the December meeting as it assesses the recent flow of data and then remain on hold into next year'; 'we had been thinking that the RBA would not start cutting until November next year, but the weakening jobs market mean it could now come earlier say around August'. Recession risk put at 'a high and still rising 40%'. 25bp cut size assumed

ABC (25 Nov, after October CPI at 4.9%): 'Economists at UBS, on the other hand, still expect the RBA to cut interest rates in August 2027'; UBS sees some risk of a February hike, but the board split with 'dovish external board members' makes a hike unlikely. Earlier, George Tharenou (19 Nov): 'We now expect the first rate cut of -25bps in Aug-27 (was Nov-27)' and 'an easing cycle of -75bps'. December hold inferred

Goldman Sachs (Pound Sterling Live, 20 Nov, new outlook; analyst not named): cash rate held at 4.85% 'until the fourth quarter of 2027', then lowered to 3.6% by end-2028; market pricing of about 4.4% called 'too hawkish'. Earlier (17 Nov): says the cash rate has peaked. December hold inferred. Month (November, first Q4 2027 meeting) and 25bp first-cut size assumed

Tim Hext (19 Nov): no explicit December call; 'The Reserve Bank is achieving much earlier than expected what it set out to do with the five rate hikes this year' and 'will be cautious until inflation starts turning'; notes markets price a full cut by August 2027 and 'If rate cuts begin next year the cycle will be deeper than just two cuts'. No own timing published. Earlier, Steve Campbell (3 Nov): 'Further tightening can't be ruled out'
